message.content: Found the failing run – it breaks in_arena at step 65. I'll shrink it to a minimal case and begin triage.
Shrunk to a minimal 33-step case that still leaves the arena. I'll replay it to confirm and inspect the failure sequence.
The scene is clear: a fast body collides and drives another past the arena wall. I'll trace the collision timeline to pinpoint the failure.
I've identified the cause: a high-speed transfer leaves the body moving too fast for the boundary to contain. I'll test a counterfactual to verify.

**Ledger:**
- Open: in_arena overshoot after high-speed body-body momentum transfer
- Ruled out: wall tunneling (distance stays >0, wall is interior thin wall not arena boundary), NaN, etc.

**Hypothesis:** Body 1 (27.7 m/s) bounces off floor/wall then collides with body 0 at ~step27, transferring ~30.64 m/s to body 0. Body 0 then travels to x≈19.45 in ~6 steps, so its centre+radius exceeds arena width 20 + 0.15 tolerance. Sub-stepping (18 substeps) is insufficient to prevent overshoot / boundary impulse fails at this speed.

Shunk & replay confirmed identical trace.

Inspected timeline: body 0 static until step 26, collision at 27 giving vx 30.64, then continuous motion to violation at 33.

Counterfactual: reduce body 1 initial vx 27.7 → 5 keeps system below escape velocity and passes.
